{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 treated PDB 1acc chain A, anthrax protective antigen, as one whole-chain domain: d1acca_ (SUNID 43828; A:), family f.11.1.1, superfamily f.11.1, fold f.11, all named “Anthrax protective antigen,” in class f, “Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides.” This definition persisted in SCOPe 2.03. The release endpoints show the split in 2.04, retained through the current release, 2.08:

• d1acca2 (SUNID 238522), A:14–225: PA14 family b.179.1.1, PA14-like superfamily b.179.1, Anthrax protective antigen N-terminal-like fold b.179, in class b, “All beta proteins.”
• d1acca1 (SUNID 238521), A:226–735: Anthrax protective antigen C-terminal-like family f.60.1.1, superfamily f.60.1, and fold f.60, in class f.

This is a revised evolutionary partition of the same protein, not a physical change in its structure. A single polypeptide can contain modules with distinct evolutionary relationships; treating the entire chain as one domain can obscure those relationships. In particular, the N-terminal region can be compared with PA14-like domains independently of the remaining protective-antigen architecture. The split does not establish that the two regions are homologous to each other, independently functional, or the only possible structural subdivisions. Family membership supports relatively close homology; superfamily membership supports more remote common ancestry. Sharing a fold alone does not establish homology, and class membership is broader still.

Homology searches should therefore use the revised domain boundaries and separate domain sequences or profiles, or interpret whole-chain hits by their aligned region and domain coverage. A PA14-like match supports a relationship for that module; it does not establish whole-chain homology, the presence of the C-terminal module, or protective-antigen/toxin function. Likewise, a structural template matching one domain supports modeling that region, not automatically the whole chain. Select representatives for each relevant domain family or superfamily, preserve release-specific identifiers and boundaries, and remap old d1acca_ hits before comparing historical results.
